title: Ability to sort (and paginate) by column
body:
As requested in https://github.com/simonw/datasette/issues/185#issuecomment-376614973

I've previously avoided this for performance reasons: sort-by-column on a column without an index is likely to perform badly for hundreds of thousands of rows.

That's not a good enough reason to avoid the feature entirely though. A few options:

* Allow sort-by-column by default, give users the option to disable it for specific tables/columns
* Disallow sort-by-column by default, give users option (probably in `metadata.json`) to enable it for specific tables/columns
* Automatically detect if a column either has an index on it OR a table has less than X rows in it

We already have the mechanism in place to cut off SQL queries that take more than X seconds, so if someone DOES try to sort by a column that's too expensive it won't actually hurt anything - but it would be nice to not show people a "sort" option which is guaranteed to throw a timeout error.

The vast majority of datasette usage that I've seen so far is on smaller datasets where the performance penalties of sort-by-column are extremely unlikely to show up.

----

Still left to do:

title: `datasette create-token` ability to create tokens with a reduced set of permissions
body:
Initial design ideas: https://github.com/simonw/datasette/issues/1852#issuecomment-1289733483

> Token design concept:
> 
> ```json
> {
>     "t": {
>         "a": ["ir", "ur", "dr"],
>         "d": {
>             "fixtures": ["ir", "ur", "dr"]
>         },
>         "t": {
>             "fixtures": {
>                 "searchable": ["ir"]
>             }
>         }
>     }
> }
> ```
> 
> That JSON would be minified and signed.
> 
> Minified version of the above looks like this (101 characters):
> 
> `{"t":{"a":["ir","ur","dr"],"d":{"fixtures":["ir","ur","dr"]},"t":{"fixtures":{"searchable":["ir"]}}}}`
> 
> The `"t"` key shows this is a token that as a default API key.
> 
> `"a"` means "all" - these are permissions that have been granted on all tables and databases.
> 
> `"d"` means "databases" - this is a way to set permissions for all tables in a specific database.
> 
> `"t"` means "tables" - this lets you set permissions at a finely grained table level.
> 
> Then the permissions themselves are two character codes which are shortened versions - so:
> 
> * `ir` = `insert-row`
> * `ur` = `update-row`
> * `dr` = `delete-row`

title: Test suite cleanup: move older tests to `datasette.client`, parametrize duplicates
body:
I had Fable 5.2 audit the test suite - in addition to the fixes I shipped in 8666758d923117642128e03fe1db032f61eeda11 and b92e31988250b8756a2c0131a4f82b00b1f1b03a and 9dc86753bb8c9070c02081fadc2070ac67a43fb6 and 61a81b62eb52e04ca2372ef8d0daebe6f4c58839 it made the following suggestions.

Initial prompt:

> Before `datasette.client` existed this test suite used other mechanisms for the tests - since `datasette.client` most tests have used that instead
> 
> Do an audit of the test suite and look for opportunities to refactor older tests to use `datasette.client` - and while you are doing that, look out for performance boosts to the tests and also tests that could be combined cleanly using pytest.mark.parametrize

<details><summary>Claude Fable 5.2 Medium</summary>

Follow-up from an audit of the test suite. The main performance problem it found (the slow fixture database writer) is already fixed, along with two warnings and a plugin-leak ordering bug. This issue tracks what was found but not done.

## 1. Move older tests from `TestClient` to `datasette.client`

About 150 call sites in 13 files still use the sync `TestClient` from `datasette.utils.testing`, mostly through `make_app_client()` or the `app_client*` session fixtures in `tests/fixtures.py`. The suite has 543 sync tests and 1,195 async ones (not every sync test uses a client).

| File | Sync-client calls | `make_app_client()` calls |
|---|---|---|
| `test_html.py` | 37 | 15 |
| `test_permissions.py` | 22 | 12 |
| `test_table_api.py` | 18 | 12 |
| `test_plugins.py` | 16 | 8 |
| `test_api.py` | 16 | 1 |
| `test_table_html.py` | 15 | 9 |
| `test_auth.py` | 9 | 0 |
| `test_tracer.py` | 5 | 4 |
| `test_stored_queries.py` | via fixtures | 3 |

`test_csv.py`, `test_csrf_middleware.py`, `test_crossdb.py`, `test_facets.py` and `test_custom_pages.py` have a handful each.

They fall into four groups:

Differences to watch when porting:

- `.status` becomes `.status_code`, and `.json` becomes `.json()`.
- `post(path, {...}, csrftoken_from=True)` becomes `post(path, data={...})`. `csrftoken_from` appears 14 times and is already a no-op.
- `if_none_match=` becomes an `if-none-match` header.

Leave alone: `test_cli.py` (it uses `CliRunner`), and at least one test of `TestClient` itself, since plugins may still import it.

## 2. Parametrize candidates

Found by comparing test bodies structurally. "Checked" means the tests were read and confirmed to differ only in the listed values; the others are structural matches that still need a look.

| File | Tests | Varies by | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_column_types.py` | 9 validation tests (insert, update, upsert) | path, JSON body, status, error column | yes |
| `test_error_shape.py` | 8 "400 with this error" tests, plus 4 similar 404s | path, expected error | yes |
| `test_plugins.py` | 6 `test_hook_top_*` | path, expected fragment | yes |
| `test_plugins.py` | 3 `test_hook_render_cell_pks_*` | path, expected pks | yes |
| `test_utils_sql_analysis.py` | 6 `test_analyze_*_tables` | SQL, params, expected operations | yes |
| `test_custom_pages.py` | 3 status/text tests and 3 redirect tests | path, status, text or location | yes |
| `test_csrf_middleware.py` | 3 origin scheme/port tests | headers, scheme, outcome | yes |
| `test_api.py` | 3 row JSON tests | path, expected rows | yes |
| `test_table_html.py` | `test_metadata_sort` and `test_metadata_sort_desc`, 32 lines each | table, headers, rows | yes |
| `test_table_api.py` | 10 shape, expand-label and infinity tests | path, expected JSON | no |
| `test_csv.py` | 5 "get path, compare body" tests; CSV/TSV download pair | path, expected text | no |
| `test_multipart.py` | 3 bad content-type tests | header, error | no |
| `test_cli.py` | `test_install` / `test_uninstall` | command | no |

Probably not worth combining: the `test_autocomplete.py` tests share a shape but each builds a different schema, and the 50-line pair in `test_restriction_sql.py` looks like the same scenario run deliberately through two APIs.

## 3. Smaller items

## Context

Serial suite time on macOS after the fixture writer fix is about 86s (down from 261s). The slowest remaining tests are the subprocess ones in `test_pytest_autoclose_plugin.py` and `test_cli_serve_server.py` at roughly 1s each, which is inherent to what they do.

</details>
reference: **Direct swap to `ds_client`.** Tests that use plain `app_client` for HTTP: `test_logout` and the create-token tests in `test_auth.py`, the three legacy-csrftoken tests in `test_csrf_middleware.py`, the column-statistics tests in `test_html.py` and `test_table_html.py`, and `test_permissions_checked`.
**Only need a `Datasette` object.** Eight tests and the `db` fixture in `test_internals_database.py` take `app_client` just for `.ds`.

**Custom settings or config only.** Most of the ~70 `make_app_client(settings=...)` / `config=...` calls. These want an async factory fixture that mirrors `ds_client` in `conftest.py` (in-memory fixtures database plus keyword overrides). That costs about 60ms and touches no disk.
**Need a real file.** Immutable databases, `inspect_data`, the dotted filename, `extra_databases`, crossdb and database download. These stay on disk but can make requests through `client.ds.client`.

`make_app_client()` calls `os.chdir()` into a temporary directory that is deleted when the context manager exits, leaving the process in a directory that no longer exists. Moving tests off `make_app_client()` (section 1) reduces exposure; the `chdir` itself may be removable.
`app_client_returned_rows_matches_page_size` in `tests/fixtures.py` appears to be unused and can be deleted.
